clearing_status.fact: The SEC granted ONE formal one-year extension on Feb 25 2025 (Exchange Act Release No. 34-102487), moving cash clearing to Dec 31 2026 and repo clearing to Jun 30 2027. As of the SEC commissioner August 2026 update (sec.gov, ~Aug 7 2026), those dates remain unchanged and no second extension has been announced; however, SIFMA and IIB exemptive-relief requests are actively pending before the Commission (published Apr 17 2026), comment periods on combined inter-affiliate/extraterritorial relief and a 15c3-3 net-omnibus margin exemption closed Aug 31 2026, and the SEC has granted conditional exemptive relief for captive clearing subsidiaries for private funds - all consistent with multiple open exemptive-relief requests still pending.
clearing_status.rationale: Rubric level 1 requires 'an official extension granted OR exemptive-relief requests pending': the Feb 2025 one-year extension is an official granted extension (the first formal deadline push), and multiple SIFMA/IIB exemptive-relief requests remain pending as of Aug 2026. No second formal extension has been announced, so level 2 is not warranted.

plan_financing.fact: The 10-year JGB yield closed at ~2.88% on 21 Aug 2026 and intra-week touched 2.95% — levels last seen in 1996 — driven by fiscal uncertainty around the Takaichi administration's FY2027 budget planning and continued supplementary-budget debt concerns. That represents a rise of roughly +60-70 bps from the ~2.1-2.2% range seen in Feb-Mar 2026, and +87 bps from the ~2.0% level when Takaichi first took office. The most recent JGB auction data shows the 5-year sale on 18 Aug 2026 cleared with a bid-to-cover of 4.15 (strong), while the MOF 20-year auction on 20 Aug 2026 cleared without a reported failure. No BOJ emergency operation has been cited. Funding path for the upcoming FY2027 budget remains unspecified amid markets 'bracing for next phase of fiscal planning' (Nikkei Asia, 19 Aug 2026). Oxford Economics noted the 10y yield 'risen sharply from 2.1% in March, fuelled by market concern about Japan's more aggressive fiscal stance' (Oxford Economics, Jun 2026). Sources: TradingEconomics (22 Aug 2026), Nikkei Asia (19 Aug 2026), Bloomberg (18 Aug 2026), Oxford Economics (Jun 2026).
plan_financing.rationale: The 10-year JGB yield has risen well over 50 bps from its early-2026 baseline on fiscal concerns, but auctions continue to clear (5y BTC 4.15, no failed auction cited) and no BOJ emergency operation has been triggered; the FY2027 fiscal/funding path remains unspecified. This pattern — large yield move on fiscal news, auctions still clearing, no disorderly failure — maps squarely to rubric level 1 (UNCLEAR: funding path unspecified OR >25 bps yield move on fiscal news but auctions still clearing).

direct_lending_default.fact: Fitch Ratings' July 2026 US Corporate Distressed and Default Monitor reported the trailing 12-month private credit default rate (inclusive of distressed exchanges and LMEs) reached approximately 6.1%, a new record high, up from 6.0% in Q2 2026. Source: Bloomberg 2026-07-30 (https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-07-30/fitch-s-private-credit-default-rate-hit-record-in-second-quarter) and cryptobriefing.com summary of Fitch July 2026 monitor (https://cryptobriefing.com/fitch-us-corporate-default-rates-july-2026/).
direct_lending_default.rationale: The Fitch inclusive TTM private-credit default rate (counting distressed exchanges and LMEs) ticked up to 6.1% in July 2026 from the prior record of 6.0% set in Q2; this is applied directly as the rubric-anchored Fitch inclusive measure, with the July 2026 Fitch publication as the as_of period. One LinkedIn snippet from Fitch's own page cited '5.2% in July' but context suggests this references a sub-index (possibly PMR or count-based), not the headline inclusive TTM rate that Bloomberg and CryptoBriefing confirm at 6.1%.

dissent.view: With Intelligence estimated the 'true' private credit default rate (inclusive of selective defaults and LMEs) approached ~5% through 9M 2025, materially below the concurrent Fitch inclusive reading
Moody's noted ~65% of 2025 private credit defaults were distressed restructurings; excluding them yields headline rates of 1.6%-4.7%
Fitch LinkedIn post title references '5.2% in July' — possibly a sub-index or count-based variant, not the headline inclusive TTM rate

redemption_gates.fact: Fitch Ratings tracked 10 of 16 non-traded BDCs breaching their 5%-of-NAV quarterly repurchase caps in Q2 2026; Robert A. Stanger & Co. recorded repurchase requests at 12.4% of NAV (highest on record), with sponsors fulfilling only 38% and leaving ~$9.6B unfilled. Named gating funds in Q2 include: Blackstone BCRED (~$79B NAV), BlackRock HPS Corporate Lending Fund (~$26B), Blue Owl Credit Income Corp (~$34B), Blue Owl Technology Income Corp (OTIC, 38.1% request rate), Apollo Debt Solutions, and Cliffwater CCLFX. Blue Owl OBDC II ($1.6B) permanently closed redemptions in Q1 2026. Sources: Fitch Ratings via angelinvestorsnetwork.com (2026-08-20); Robert A. Stanger & Co. via tradingmarketsignals.com (2026-08-17); whitesecuritieslaw.com (July 2026); wildscrew.wordpress.com citing Bloomberg (2026-07-02).
redemption_gates.rationale: Named gating/capped funds in Q2 2026 number well above 3 and their combined AUM (BCRED ~$79B + HPS ~$26B + OCIC ~$34B alone = ~$139B) far exceeds the $100B rubric threshold, with Fitch confirming 10 of 16 tracked BDCs breaching caps in the same quarter -- a clear WIDESPREAD (2) classification.

dissent.view: Some analysts (CLA Wealth Advisors, CAIA, PGIM) argue funds are 'operating as designed' within contractual caps, not in crisis, and that request spikes reflect sentiment rather than credit deterioration -- implying the word 'gating' overstates structural stress.
Early Q3 2026 data (Golub GCRED cleared July 29 tender in full; three NAV BDCs showing 4.6% requests vs 7.9% in Q2) suggest the redemption wave may be peaking and stress is easing as of August 2026.

new_imf_programs.fact: IMF Executive Board approved a new 48-month EFF for Ukraine (US$8.1bn) on 26 Feb 2026 (imf.org/en/news/articles/2026/02/26/pr-26066). A staff-level EFF agreement with Bolivia was reached 29 Jul 2026 (imf.org/en/news/articles/2026/07/29/pr26268) but Board approval is still pending as of the search date. No sovereign missed coupon or formal default has been identified in the Feb-Aug 2026 window; Argentina and Ecuador are in ongoing program reviews, not new arrangements.
new_imf_programs.rationale: One fully Board-approved new IMF arrangement (Ukraine, Feb 26 2026) falls in the trailing 6-month window; Bolivia is staff-level only and does not yet constitute an executed program under a 'talk vs. action' standard. One confirmed new program with no missed coupons maps to RISING (band 1) under the rubric.

dissent.view: If Bolivia's Board approval occurred before 2026-08-24 but was not captured in available search results, the count would rise to 2 and the rating would be CLUSTER (value=2).

china_ppi.fact: NBS official press release (stats.gov.cn/english/PressRelease/202608/t20260810_1965017.html, released 2026-08-10): 'In July 2026, China's producer price index for industrial products (PPI) increased by 3.5% year on year and decreased by 0.7% month on month.' Corroborated by Xinhua (2026-08-09) and China Daily (2026-08-09).
china_ppi.rationale: The signed figure is +3.5% YoY for July 2026, released by NBS on 2026-08-10; rubric scores on SIZE of move — at +3.5% this represents a notable cost-push signal that has reversed a prolonged deflation streak, flagging potential input-cost pressure spillover to trading partners.

trade_actions.fact: At least 6 new major-economy trade measures against China (or by China) in trailing 3 months: (1) USTR new 12.5% Section 301 tariff on ALL Chinese goods effective 24 Jul 2026 (China-Briefing, 23 Jul 2026 update; https://www.china-briefing.com/news/us-china-tariff-rates-2025/); (2) EU definitive anti-dumping duty on Chinese polyamide yarns (Regulation EU 2026/1823, 28 Jul 2026; cambioslegales.es); (3) China MOFCOM provisional anti-dumping deposits up to 54.3% on US/Mexican pecans, effective 11 Aug 2026 (Global Times/MOFCOM); (4) China MOFCOM+MOF export control and procurement bans on 56 US entities, 22 Jun 2026 (Arnold & Porter); (5) China export bans on 14 EU defense/tech/chemical companies, ~3 Aug 2026 (Mondaq/Steptoe); (6) China MOFCOM national security investigation into imported printing/copying equipment, 5 Aug 2026 (MOFCOM Announcement No. 33 of 2026).
trade_actions.rationale: Six distinct new trade measures across three major economies in the trailing 3 months exceeds the rubric threshold of >=4 for ESCALATING; the USTR 12.5% action alone also qualifies as a broad tariff round (>=10% across a sector -- here all Chinese goods), satisfying two independent ESCALATING triggers.

dissent.view: Some analysts characterise the USTR 12.5% Section 301 tariff as a net +2.5% effective increase (since a 10% baseline was already in force), and note the Nov 2025 US-China truce is still formally intact through Nov 2026, suggesting managed escalation rather than truce breakdown.
China frames its June 2026 entity-list actions as narrowly targeted at defense/rare-earth sectors with minimal trade disruption, signalling intent to avoid broad escalation.

license_flow.fact: The April 2025 rare-earth magnet licensing regime (covering dysprosium, terbium and magnets containing them) is fully in force and was never suspended. MOFCOM's statutory target is 45 working days (~9 weeks), but industry reporting (GetTransport/Duramag, July 2026) shows heavy-REE magnet approvals routinely run 60-120+ days. General licences exist but are limited to a small whitelist of pre-cleared Chinese exporters (first batch: JL MAG, San Huan, Yunsheng, Dec 2025); the scheme 'is not broadly available yet.' In June 2026 China added 10 US firms to its export control list (Morgan Lewis, July 1 2026), and Trump threatened 200% tariffs in August 2026 over continued supply delays (China Briefing, Aug 2026). The 2026 licensing catalogue added samarium, gadolinium and lutetium compounds as new controlled categories (Certivo, Mar 2026). No categorical denial or suspension of licensing has been announced.
license_flow.rationale: The regime is case-by-case for most shippers (general licences confined to a narrow whitelist), processing times structurally exceed 30 days (60-120 days in practice), and new categories were added to the control list within the trailing 3 months — all squarely within rubric level 1 (SLOWING). No announced categorical denial or licensing suspension exists to justify level 2. [cross-check (asi1): two reads disagreed (1 vs 0); held for review]

dissent.view: MERICS (undated 2025/2026) notes a MOFCOM 'green channel' and EU whitelist have allowed magnet exports to the EU to pick up since May 2025, suggesting some easing for civilian buyers; this could be read as partial normalisation toward level 0 for EU-bound civilian flows.
Rare Earth Exchanges (Apr 2026) cites licensing approval rates below 25% for European firms, which some analysts characterise as functionally approaching level 2 for certain end-users or sectors.

truce_status.fact: The Nov-2025 US-China minerals truce (formal expiry Nov 10, 2026) remains nominally in force but is fraying: on June 22 2026 China's MOFCOM added 10 US entities—including MP Materials and USA Rare Earth—to its export control blacklist (partial breach); as of Aug 21 2026 <90 days remain with no renewal signal. Source: Modern Diplomacy 2026-08-21 citing Reuters 2026a; Benchmark Minerals 2026-06-25; FDD 2026-06-24; White House Fact Sheet 2025-11-01.
truce_status.rationale: Two rubric triggers for Score 1 are both met: (a) <90 days to the Nov 10 2026 nominal expiry with no extension announced, and (b) a partial breach via new entity-list additions on June 22 2026. Score 2 is capped because the broad suspension has not been formally cancelled and analysts describe the entity actions as largely symbolic with limited direct economic impact.

dissent.view: FDD (2026-06-24) characterises the June 22 entity-list actions as ending 'the pause', implying Score 2; however this is contradicted by the blanket suspension remaining formally in place and Reuters/Benchmark analysts calling the measures narrow and symbolic.

re_blacklist.fact: China MOFCOM Announcement No. 23 of 2026 (issued 22 June 2026) added 10 named US entities to its export-control list under the Export Control Law and Dual-Use Items Regulations, explicitly including MP Materials Corp and USA Rare Earth. The restriction is firm-specific: Chinese companies and individuals are barred from supplying dual-use goods to these named entities. Multiple corroborating sources (Benchmark Minerals, Arnold & Porter, Al Jazeera, Bloomberg, ORF, The Oregon Group) confirm the listing date and named firms. Market reaction was muted -- MP Materials was roughly flat and USA Rare Earth modestly higher on the announcement day -- consistent with a targeted, entity-level action rather than a sector-wide shock.
re_blacklist.rationale: Both MP Materials and USA Rare Earth are explicitly named on MOFCOM Announcement No. 23 of 2026 (22 June 2026), satisfying rubric level 1 (entity-specific listing of named US producers). All authoritative sources, including Benchmark Minerals and Arnold & Porter, characterise the measure as entity-specific rather than a blanket or sector-wide restriction, ruling out level 2.

hree_premium.fact: As of August 17, 2026, Rare Earth Exchanges reports terbium assessed at $3,600–$5,000+/kg in Western markets vs ~$989–998/kg China domestic (implying ~3.6x–5.0x), while Argus data cited by Reuters (Oregon Group, June 2026) puts dysprosium and terbium oxide ex-China prices at 4x–5x Chinese domestic references; Benchmark Minerals (March 2026) pegged 2025 dysprosium CIF North America at 4.4x EXW China.
hree_premium.rationale: Multiple corroborating price-signal sources (Argus/Reuters, Benchmark, RareEarthExchanges, S&P Global Platts) place the heavy rare earth ex-China premium in the 4–5x range for the primary magnet HREEs (dysprosium, terbium) as of mid-to-late 2026, anchored by actual transaction data and export volume declines (~50% shipping drop per Chinese customs); best single estimate is ~4.5x as the central tendency across sources, consistent with the volume signal confirming genuine supply bifurcation rather than a paper premium.

dissent.view: Project Blue Group / Discovery Alert (May 2026) implies only ~2.6x premium using monazite concentrate basket pricing (non-Chinese 60% TREO at $16,000–19,000/t vs China $6,142/t) — significantly lower because it blends light and heavy REEs, diluting the HREE-specific multiple
Serra Verde–USA Rare Earth contractual floors ($575/kg Dy, $2,050/kg Tb) imply only ~2x Chinese reference prices, but these are long-term contracted floors, not spot market levels
Benchmark Minerals forecasts the multiple will nearly double to 8.3x by 2027, suggesting current 2026 mid-year is in transition above 4.4x (2025 baseline) but not yet at 2027 peak

genius_impl.fact: The statutory deadline for federal agencies to issue final GENIUS Act implementing rules was July 18, 2026. As of August 24, 2026, every major implementing rule — OCC (NPRM Feb 25/Mar 2 2026), FDIC (NPRM Apr 7 2026), Treasury/FinCEN/OFAC (NPRMs Apr–Aug 2026) — remains at the proposed/comment stage with no final rules issued. ABA Banking Journal (Aug 2026) states: 'Congress gave federal regulators until July 18, 2026, to finalize the Genius Act\'s implementing rules. That deadline came and went without a coordinated final package.' Tech-Insider (Jul 24 2026) confirms: 'Every major GENIUS implementing rule across the OCC, FDIC, Treasury, FinCEN, and OFAC is still pending finalization.' Sources: ABA Banking Journal (https://bankingjournal.aba.com/2026/08/aba-viewpoint-the-genius-act-rules-are-almost-here-heres-what-banks-should-do/), tech-insider.org (https://tech-insider.org/genius-act-stablecoin-law/), FDIC.gov (https://www.fdic.gov/news/financial-institution-letters/2026/notice-proposed-rulemaking-establish-genius-act), OCC.gov (https://www.occ.gov/news-issuances/bulletins/2026/bulletin-2026-3.html), Treasury (https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0605).
genius_impl.rationale: The rubric scores 2 = PROBLEMS when the statutory deadline is missed without final rules issued. The July 18, 2026 deadline has passed and all major agency implementing rules (OCC, FDIC, Treasury, FinCEN, OFAC) remain in the proposed/comment stage as of August 24, 2026, with no final rule package published. No court stay or compliance-failure event is documented, but the missed deadline without finalization is unambiguous and meets the rubric's level-2 criterion.

ai_revenue_gap.fact: Q2 2026 earnings: combined hyperscaler 2026 capex guidance raised to ~$730B (~+78% YoY vs ~$410B in 2025); Alphabet Q2 capex $44.9B (~+~100% YoY), Microsoft FY26 cash capex +80% YoY, Meta Q2 capex $31.08B (+83% YoY), Amazon 2026 capex raised to ~$220B. Meanwhile AI-attributable cloud revenue accelerated QoQ: Google Cloud +82% YoY in Q2 (vs +63% Q1), AWS +37% YoY (vs +28% Q1), Azure +43% YoY (vs +40% Q1); AWS AI business annualized >$25B 'more than doubling YoY' (CNBC/Amazon Q2 2026 earnings, July 30 2026; Alphabet Q2 2026 earnings release, SEC, July 22 2026). UBS estimates hyperscalers will spend ~102% of cloud revenue on capex in 2026 (Yahoo Finance, Aug 2026).
ai_revenue_gap.rationale: Capex growth (~78–100%+ YoY) materially exceeds AI-revenue growth in growth-rate terms, satisfying the WIDE condition; however, AI-attributable cloud revenue is accelerating QoQ across all four hyperscalers and no company cut its AI-revenue outlook — ruling out the WIDENING FAST (2) classification which requires deceleration or an outlook cut.

gpu_refi_stress.fact: CoreWeave's 5-year CDS spread hit ~855 bps on July 29 2026 (implying ~50% cumulative default probability); its $2.6B GPU-backed loan facility closed August 10 2026 only after spreads flexed 125 bps to clear; and the company carries a documented $4.2B refinancing wall on pre-2026 GPU-collateralized debt against sharply depreciated H100 collateral (-70-90% rental rates). PIMCO moved to sell >$14B of Oracle-linked AI data center debt in secondary markets. Sources: TechTimes 2026-07-30, TechTimes 2026-08-03, CoreWeave IR 2026-08-10, Global Data Center Hub 2026-07-08.
gpu_refi_stress.rationale: CoreWeave is a named borrower explicitly facing a 2026 refinancing wall with CDS at distressed-borrower levels (855 bps/50% default odds), and AI data center debt is being offloaded at a discount in secondary markets (PIMCO/Oracle-linked paper) — both are rubric-1 triggers. No confirmed default, distressed exchange, or outright failed refinancing has been documented as of 2026-08-24, so rubric-2 is not met.

dissent.view: CoreWeave successfully closed a $2.6B loan facility on August 10 2026 and a prior $2B bond was heavily oversubscribed in May 2026, suggesting lenders remain willing to extend GPU-backed credit at scale, which sits in tension with a 50% implied default probability.

cmbs_office_delinq.fact: Trepp CMBS office delinquency rate hit a new all-time high of 11.76% in October 2025, per CommercialSearch/Trepp data (https://www.commercialsearch.com/news/cmbs-delinquency-rates/). The July 2026 Trepp overall CMBS rate rose to 7.86% (+51 bps) with office towers among the largest newly delinquent loans, but no public Trepp office sub-rate for July 2026 was available in accessible summaries.
cmbs_office_delinq.rationale: The rubric calls for the latest published Trepp CMBS office delinquency percent; 11.76% is the most recent explicitly cited Trepp office sub-rate in public sources (Oct 2025). The July 2026 data likely exceeds this given large new office delinquencies, but no confirmed figure was retrievable, warranting medium confidence on the Oct 2025 anchor. [vintage guard: new read is 2025-10-31 data but the prior applied value was 2026-03 data; kept the newer vintage]

dissent.view: KBRA-rated CMBS office delinquency rate was 13.9% in January 2026 (rose 156 bps that month), a materially higher figure but reflects a different rated universe than Trepp's broader dataset
S&P Global headline for January 2026 states 'The Office Rate Surpasses 10.5%' for US CMBS, consistent with Trepp range but a separate methodology

regional_bank_stress.fact: Four US bank failures in 2026 as of July 17, 2026 (FDIC failed-bank list, last updated July 17, 2026): Metropolitan Capital Bank & Trust ($261M, Jan 30), Community Bank & Trust – West Georgia ($288M, May 1), Kentland Federal Savings and Loan ($3.7M, Jul 10), Small Business Bank ($73M, Jul 17). All are sub-$10B institutions. Bisnow (Feb 2, 2026) found real-estate loan exposure as a contributing factor in the Metropolitan Capital failure; FDIC issued an enforcement action against Community Bank & Trust – West Georgia in April 2026 prior to its closure (Forbes Advisor). No failure exceeded $10B in assets and no interagency emergency CRE supervisory action was identified.
regional_bank_stress.rationale: At least one failure (Metropolitan Capital) carries credible CRE/real-estate exposure linkage per Bisnow's court-record review, and the FDIC enforcement action preceding Community Bank & Trust's closure qualifies as a public enforcement action under the rubric — mapping squarely to ISOLATED (1). The cluster threshold (>=3 CRE-attributed failures, any >$10B, or coordinated interagency action) is not met. [cross-check (asi1): two reads disagreed (1 vs 0); held for review]

dissent.view: FDIC has not publicly named CRE concentration as a formal cause for any 2026 failure; the CRE link for Metropolitan Capital is based on Bisnow's review of court records, not an official FDIC/Fed/OCC statement, which could support a CALM (0) reading if only official FDIC attributions are counted.

govt_stability.fact: PM Sébastien Lecornu's second minority government (formed 10 Oct 2025) remains incumbent. It survived four no-confidence votes (Oct 16 2025, Jan 14 2026, Feb 2 2026 x2), invoked Article 49.3 on Jan 20 2026 to force the 2026 budget, and the budget passed Feb 2 2026. Sources: France 24 (20 Jan 2026), Al Jazeera (2 Feb 2026), Euronews (23 Jan 2026), Wikipedia Lecornu governments.
govt_stability.rationale: The government is a self-described 'fragile minority' coalition in a hung parliament, surviving via Socialist abstentions and Article 49.3 — the textbook definition of rubric band 1. No confidence vote has been lost, no PM resignation since Oct 6 2025 (resolved by re-appointment), and no snap election has been called, ruling out band 2.

rating_action.fact: S&P Global Ratings downgraded France from 'AA-' to 'A+' (stable outlook) on ~17 October 2025 (spglobal.com article dated Oct 17 2025: 'France Ratings Lowered To A+/A-1 From AA-/A-1+'). Fitch had already downgraded France from AA- to A+ (stable outlook) on 12 September 2025 (France24, CNBC, ING Think, Sep 13-15 2025). Moody's on 25 October 2025 kept Aa3 but moved outlook to negative (France24, Oct 25 2025).
rating_action.rationale: Two of the three major agencies (Fitch on 12 Sep 2025, S&P on ~17 Oct 2025) executed actual one-notch rating cuts from AA- to A+ within the trailing 12 months; rubric 2 requires only one actual cut in the trailing 12 months, which is clearly satisfied. Moody's negative-outlook action is subsumed by the higher severity of the executed downgrades.

subprime_auto_dpd.fact: The subprime 60-day-plus delinquency rate in June 2026 was 5.67%, down 64 basis points year-over-year, per Fitch Ratings subprime auto ABS index (Wolf Street, August 13, 2026, citing Fitch). Peak was 6.90% in January 2026.
subprime_auto_dpd.rationale: Fitch Ratings ABS index is the canonical primary source for subprime auto 60+ day delinquency; the June 2026 reading of 5.67% is the most recently reported figure and maps directly to the rubric's requested percent.

dissent.view: 6.90% in January 2026 (all-time record high per Fitch ABS index) — some sources anchor to this figure as the 'current' level without citing subsequent months
6.80% in February 2026 per Fitch ABS index — cited by TradingEconomics as the most recent figure as of their April 2026 update

bnpl_delinq.fact: Affirm FQ2'26 Shareholder Letter (filed Feb 6, 2026, period ended Dec 31, 2025): '30+ day delinquencies excluding Peloton and Pay in X loans increased 18 basis points year over year and decreased 7 basis points quarter over quarter to 2.7%.' Allowance for credit losses 5.4% of loans held for investment. Industry BNPL charge-off rate per CFPB/Richmond Fed: 1.83% in 2023, estimated ~1.8-2% in 2024-25 (well below 3%). BTIG Research (~Aug 21, 2026) separately flagged Affirm ABS 30-59 DPD at all-time highs for newest vintages.
bnpl_delinq.rationale: Affirm 30+ DPD rose +18 bps YoY to 2.7% -- up but far short of the 100 bps spike threshold for level 2; industry charge-offs remain ~1.8-2%, below the 3% containment ceiling, squarely fitting rubric level 1 (RISING, charge-offs contained). BTIG's all-time-high ABS vintage flag is a leading indicator of further deterioration but does not yet produce a reported figure breaching the level-2 thresholds.

dissent.view: BTIG Research (Aug 21, 2026) reports Affirm ABS 30-59 DPD at all-time highs for newest 2025-X2 vintage at 9 and 16 months of age, suggesting trend may be accelerating toward level 2 if it continues into H2 2026
Statista citing Affirm data through Q2 2025 showed a YoY decrease in 30+ DPD at that snapshot, suggesting the direction was briefly stable/improving before reversing

dollar_reserve_share.fact: IMF COFER Data Brief (published July 1, 2026): 'The share of US dollar holdings in foreign exchange reserves increased to 57.13 percent in 2026Q1, from 56.42 percent in 2025Q4.' Source: https://data.imf.org/en/news/imf%20data%20brief%20july%201
dollar_reserve_share.rationale: The rubric requires the latest USD share of allocated global FX reserves as a percent; the IMF COFER Data Brief dated July 1, 2026 directly supplies 57.13% for 2026Q1, which is the most recent official release as of 2026-08-24. The value maps mechanically to the rubric with no ambiguity.

dissent.view: coferdata.com displays USD at 56.77% with a -0.15pp change indicator, suggesting a possible Q2 2026 preliminary/interpolated estimate, but the site notes earlier quarters may include interpolated estimates and does not cite an official IMF Q2 2026 release.

weaponization_event.fact: As of mid-2026, BRICS Pay is in partial/early operational deployment — full rollout is targeted for the New Delhi BRICS summit (Sep 2026) — and The BRICS Unit gold-backed settlement token completed a small pilot (100 units, Oct 2025). The BRICS Pay pilot launch was confirmed by Russian FM Lavrov at the 2025 Rio summit as 'targeted for end-2026' (bricspayment.ru). No new sovereign reserve freeze or seizure beyond the pre-existing frozen Russian assets (~€260bn, immobilised since 2022) has been executed; EU asset confiscation remains in deliberation, not action.
weaponization_event.rationale: Active BRICS non-dollar settlement agreements and official launches (BRICS Pay partial deployment, BRICS Unit gold token pilot, Argentina-China swap extension) constitute multiple new non-dollar settlement launches and official rhetoric — squarely rubric band 1. No new sovereign reserve freeze/seizure has been executed in 2026, so band 2 is not triggered.

dissent.view: Some non-authoritative sources (informedclearly.com, watcher.guru) claim BRICS Pay is already 'fully operational' and intra-bloc local-currency trade is 67% — overstating confirmed reality; more sober sources (EBC Financial Group, aerapass.io, bricspayment.ru) note the system remains in pilot/early-deployment phase as of mid-2026 with full rollout pending the Sep 2026 summit.

EU confiscation of ~€210bn Russian assets has been actively plotted (Art.122 mechanism, Dec 2025), but Macron, ECB, and Belgian PM have all blocked outright seizure; Brookings (Jun 2025) and CFR note all options under consideration avoid outright confiscation — so this stays as deliberation, not executed action.

insurer_exits.fact: NAIC July 31 2026 report (MCAS 2018-2024, 715 carriers) finds company-initiated non-renewal rates up 96%-216% across all four US regions; Climate Cosmos (June 2026) names 13 states with active non-renewal waves (CA, FL, TX, LA, CO, GA, OK, and others); NAIC simultaneously characterises the market as 'operationally strong overall' with improved 2024 underwriting results. Florida Citizens fell to ~385k policies by Jan 2026 (lowest since 2012), signalling partial stabilisation. No top-10 insurer confirmed fully exiting a major state in 2026. Source: NAIC CIPR report Aug 5 2026 (content.naic.org); CNBC Aug 6 2026; Climate Cosmos June 18 2026.
insurer_exits.rationale: Thirteen states with documented non-renewal waves places the indicator firmly in the 5-15 state band of the rubric; the NAIC confirms multi-regional acceleration, but improved 2024 underwriting and Citizens depopulation signal partial stabilisation, and no top-10 insurer has fully exited a major state, so the level-2 triggers are not met.

dissent.view: insurance.com May 2026 survey finds only 7% of homeowners experienced cancellation/non-renewal and only 2-3% cited insurer market exit as the cause, suggesting the consumer-level impact remains modest and contained

cat_losses.fact: H1 2026 global insured natural catastrophe losses: Swiss Re Institute estimates $42bn (16% below 10-year trend of ~$66bn); Gallagher Re estimates $46bn (28% below 10-year average of $64bn); Aon estimates $47bn. No single event exceeded $10bn insured -- five consecutive quarters without a >$10bn event. Sources: Swiss Re Institute (swissre.com, ~Aug 20 2026), Gallagher Re H1 2026 NatCat Report (ajg.com/gallagherre, Jul 15 2026), Aon H1 2026 Global Cat Recap (artemis.bm, Jul 22 2026).
cat_losses.rationale: YTD insured losses of $42-47bn are materially BELOW the 10-year average (not above it, let alone >150%), and the largest single H1 2026 event was ~$5bn (U.S. SCS late-April outbreak) -- well under the $10bn threshold. Both the ELEVATED and SEVERE thresholds are unmet, mapping cleanly to NORMAL (0).

ss_reform_news.fact: The 2026 Social Security Trustees Report (SSA, issued 2026-06-09) projects OASI trust fund depletion in Q4 2032 -- one quarter earlier than the prior report -- with a 75-year actuarial deficit of 4.42% of taxable payroll (up 16% from 2025). No benefit cuts have been enacted; the Bipartisan Social Security Commission Act of 2026 (H.R. 9187) and the PROMISE Act are proposed but have not been brought to a vote. Source: https://www.ssa.gov/oact/trsum/ and https://www.ssa.gov/oact/TR/2026/tr2026.pdf
ss_reform_news.rationale: The 2026 Trustees Report materially worsens the depletion outlook (OASI date advanced, long-run deficit up 16%), meeting rubric band 1's criterion of a trustees report worsening the depletion date. No automatic cut has been triggered nor has any legislation enacting cuts been enacted, so band 2 does not apply.

dissent.view: CBO (Feb 2026) estimates the automatic cut upon depletion at 28% vs. SSA Trustees' 22%, reflecting different economic assumptions -- both agree on 2032 OASI depletion but disagree on cut magnitude.

pension_leverage_event.as_of: 2025-03-31 (latest TPR data); no 2026 episode found as of 2026-08-24
pension_leverage_event.fact: TPR Market Oversight report (data to 31 March 2025, published late 2025) states LDI market has fallen from ~£1.5tn to ~£0.7tn, rate buffers have risen to ~300 bps (vs ~150 bps pre-crisis), and daily volatility in leveraged LDI assets is 'more than 50% lower now than it was at the end of 2021'; no LDI margin crisis, forced gilt selling, or BoE/regulator intervention has been identified for 2026. Source: https://www.thepensionsregulator.gov.uk/en/document-library/research-and-analysis/market-oversight-how-well-pension-schemes-are-prepared-for-ldi-risk
pension_leverage_event.rationale: TPR's own data confirms buffers are at or above the 250-300 bps regulatory minimum and leverage is materially reduced; no 2026 regulator flagging, margin-call episode, or forced selling event has been found in any primary source, mapping cleanly to Rubric 0 (NONE). Confidence is medium rather than high because TPR data runs only to March 2025 and no 2026-specific TPR/BoE publication was located.

dissent.view: April 2025 UK 30-yr gilt yields hit 5.6% (26-yr high), described as 'stirring memories of 2022 pension crisis' — implying latent LDI stress concern, though no forced selling or regulator action was confirmed

January 2025 gilt selloff triggered LDI cash calls at some funds (XPS, Gallagher confirmed), but all eight industry players said the response was orderly — a borderline Rubric-1 signal that resolved without escalation

funded_ratio.fact: Milliman 100 Public Pension Funding Index (PPFI): funded ratio of the 100 largest U.S. public defined benefit plans slipped to 88.7% as of June 30, 2026, with plan assets of $6.116 trillion against total pension liabilities of $6.894 trillion. Source: Milliman PPFI, published July 30, 2026. https://www.milliman.com/en/insight/public-pension-funding-index-july-2026
funded_ratio.rationale: The Milliman PPFI reports 88.7% on a market-value basis for the 100 largest plans as of end-June 2026, the most current monthly data point; this maps directly to the rubric requesting a representative large-plan funded ratio as a percent. [vintage guard: new read is 2026-06-30 data but the prior applied value was FY2026 (as of 2026-07-23) data; kept the newer vintage]

dissent.view: Equable Institute 'State of Pensions 2026' projects the national average funded ratio at 85.0% for FY2026 across 253 statewide and municipal systems (published July 23, 2026); lower figure reflects a broader, smoothed-valuation universe.

interconnection_months.fact: LBNL Queued Up 2026 Edition (emp.lbl.gov/queues, June 2026): 'the median duration from IR to COD was over 5 years for projects built in 2025' - separately quantified as 61 months by the same dataset (Axis Intelligence citing LBNL 2026 Edition). A separate sub-metric of 45 months covers only the IR-to-signed-IA step.
interconnection_months.rationale: The rubric asks for the latest LBNL median queue wait in months; the headline IR-to-COD median of 61 months for projects reaching commercial operation in 2025 is the primary published figure from LBNL's Queued Up 2026 Edition, mapping directly to the indicator. The 45-month figure is a partial measure (IR to interconnection agreement only) and understates the full queue duration.

dissent.view: 45 months: median time from interconnection request to signed interconnection agreement (not full COD) in 2025, per LBNL Queued Up 2026 Edition - a partial-process metric

dc_moratoria.fact: New York Gov. Kathy Hochul signed an Executive Order on July 14, 2026, creating the nation's first statewide moratorium on new hyperscale data centers, pausing state environmental permits for up to one year for facilities at 50 MW or more (Axios / NY Governor press release, 2026-07-14). Additionally, DLA Piper reported as of July 1, 2026 that 'more than 100 local moratoria have been adopted nationwide' and 'at least 12 states have considered moratorium legislation.' Maine's legislature passed a statewide moratorium (later vetoed). South Dakota passed SB 135 enabling local bans. Multiple counties in Georgia, Virginia (Prince William County), and Texas (Hill County) enacted local pauses.
dc_moratoria.rationale: New York has a confirmed, signed, in-force statewide moratorium via executive order (July 14, 2026), satisfying the rubric's 'statewide moratorium enacted' criterion alone for level 2; the additional 100+ local moratoria nationwide and 12+ states with bills further confirm the WIDESPREAD classification. Jurisdictions with enacted pauses/moratoria include: New York (statewide EO), Maine (passed legislature, vetoed), South Dakota (local-enabling law SB 135), Georgia (multiple counties), Virginia (Prince William County invalidation), Texas Hill County (briefly enacted then rescinded), plus 100+ other local jurisdictions per DLA Piper.

dissent.view: Maine is sometimes cited as the 'first' to pass a statewide moratorium (LD 307), but Gov. Mills vetoed it in April 2026, so it never took effect; some early sources (April 2026) incorrectly describe Maine as having enacted a statewide ban.

WilmerHale (Aug 2026) states 'legislators in six states have introduced ten similar bills' at the state level, a lower count than DLA Piper's '12 states,' reflecting different cutoff dates and counting methodologies.

ai_power_pressure.fact: DOE issued emergency Section 202(c) orders to PJM three times in 2026 (most recently July 4, 2026) authorizing curtailment of data-center load onto diesel backup generators; New York Governor Hochul issued Executive Order No. 62 (July 14, 2026) imposing a statewide data-center moratorium citing grid strain; ERCOT suspended Batch Zero Large Load classification notifications on Aug 7, 2026 pending PUCT review; PUCT on July 24, 2026 affirmed full emergency curtailment authority over co-located data centers under SB 6. IEA Electricity 2026 (iea.org) confirms >2,500 GW stalled in global grid queues and 'many power systems already experiencing rising congestion-related curtailment.'
ai_power_pressure.rationale: Rubric Level 2 requires confirmed curtailment of data-center load, a declared grid emergency, or a power-scarcity-driven moratorium — all three conditions are simultaneously met: DOE/PJM emergency curtailment orders executed in 2026, New York statewide moratorium enacted July 14 2026, and ERCOT/PUCT curtailment authority formally affirmed July 24 2026. The IEA as primary source corroborates systemic congestion-related curtailment worldwide.

dissent.view: FERC June 18 2026 orders aim to 'significantly shorten the multi-year interconnection queue backlog,' suggesting regulatory relief is in motion that could ease conditions — but queues and curtailment remain active as of August 2026

mine_disruptions.fact: As of mid-to-late August 2026, at least four top-20 copper mines carry confirmed, active production cuts: (1) Grasberg (world #2) running at ~65% capacity in H2 2026 vs. pre-incident levels after Sept 2025 mudslide, with Freeport targeting only 700 million lb copper in 2026 vs. pre-incident 1.7 billion lb - mining.com, 8 May 2026; (2) Kamoa-Kakula (#3-4 globally) revised down to 290,000-330,000 t in 2026 vs. original 600,000 t target following 2025 seismic flooding - metalnomist.com, 30 May 2026; (3) Lundin's Caserones hit by two severe storms (July 18 and Aug 14 2026), guidance cut to 120,000-130,000 t from 130,000-140,000 t - mining.com, ~19 Aug 2026; (4) Codelco's Andina and El Teniente surface ops suspended by July 2026 storm, with Codelco Q2 2026 output down 14% YoY to near 28-year low; additionally Antofagasta Los Pelambres halted/curtailed - CNBC/PrimeXBT, 31 Jul 2026. Benchmark Mineral Intelligence forecast a market deficit as a direct result of these combined disruptions.
mine_disruptions.rationale: Four or more top-20 mines (Grasberg, Kamoa-Kakula, Caserones, Codelco Andina/El Teniente, Antofagasta Los Pelambres) carry confirmed active production cuts as of the rating date, well exceeding the >=3 threshold; multiple institutions (Benchmark, Goldman Sachs) have explicitly forecast a refined copper market deficit as a result, satisfying both prongs of the CLUSTER criterion.

dissent.view: Some storm disruptions (Codelco Andina, Los Pelambres) may have been temporary weather pauses lasting days rather than sustained structural outages, which could reduce the confirmed mine count slightly below 4.

copper_deficit_timing.fact: ICSG April 2026 meeting forecast: global refined copper market surplus of +96,000 metric tons in 2026, reversing its October 2025 forecast of a -150,000t deficit, driven by weaker demand growth (revised to 1.6% from 2.1%) and stronger secondary/scrap-based refined output. Source: ADMIS/IndexBox citing ICSG April 2026 Copper Market Forecast 2026/2027 (published ~April 24-28, 2026).
copper_deficit_timing.rationale: The latest ICSG forecast (April 2026) projects a +96,000t refined surplus for 2026, well above zero and unambiguously in surplus territory. Per the rubric, an official ICSG surplus forecast maps directly to score 0. [vintage guard: new read is 2026-04-24 data but the prior applied value was 2026-04 data; kept the newer vintage]

dissent.view: ICSG October 2025 forecast projected a -150,000t refined deficit for 2026 (superseded by April 2026 update)
J.P. Morgan projected a -330,000t deficit for 2026 driven by AI/hyperscale data center demand (March 2026 vintage, not updated post-ICSG flip)

drought_chip_farm.fact: According to the U.S. Drought Monitor (Drought.gov Intermountain West Status Update, August 20, 2026): 'nearly 95% of the region (Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico, Utah, and Wyoming) is experiencing some type of drought, with around 30% of the region in either Extreme Drought (D3) or Exceptional Drought (D4).' The USDA crop report (droughtmonitor.unl.edu, August 11, 2026) further notes 33% of Utah winter wheat is in poor/very poor condition vs. a 5-year average near zero, and one-half to three-quarters of rangelands in Arizona, New Mexico, and Utah are in poor/very poor condition — confirmed agricultural production impacts. No current fab water-rationing order found for Taiwan (most recent Taiwan drought impact found dates to 2021).
drought_chip_farm.rationale: D3-D4 coverage across ~30% of the US Southwest (Arizona, Utah, Colorado, New Mexico, Wyoming) meets the rubric's ACUTE threshold; confirmed agricultural production curtailment (poor/very poor crop and rangeland conditions well above historical averages) provides the required physical impact corroboration. Taiwan shows no current active water-rationing order in 2026, but the US Southwest anchor alone clears the rubric for a score of 2.

dissent.view: Arizona short-term drought picture shows some monsoon improvement in July 2026, with D2 covering 47% of state and no D3/D4 in short-term metrics for AZ specifically — suggesting intra-region variability and partial relief

reservoir_stress.fact: Lake Mead elevation 1,039.44 ft, storage 26.6% of capacity as of Aug 20 2026 (reservoirbench.com citing USBR daily gauge); USBR Lower Colorado Weekly Update (Aug 3 2026) corroborates at 1,040.96 ft / 27% of capacity. Hoover Dam minimum power pool is ~1,050 ft, placing Mead ~10-11 ft below that threshold.
reservoir_stress.rationale: Storage at ~26.6-27% of capacity is below the 30% CRITICAL threshold, independently satisfying rubric criterion 1. Elevation of ~1,039-1,041 ft is also ~9-11 ft below Hoover Dam minimum power pool (~1,050 ft), satisfying the 'within 15 feet of a power-generation threshold' criterion; both sub-criteria for rating 2 are met with confirmed physical data.

water_dispute.fact: India's Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) remains formally 'in abeyance' as of July 3, 2026 (India MEA reaffirmation, geopoliticalmonitor.com). Pakistan's defense minister stated in June 2026 that Pakistan 'will go to war' if water security is threatened, while India's water minister vowed 'not a single drop of water' will flow to Pakistan (CNBC, 2026-06-22). Pakistan's military Corps Commanders Conference issued a formal declaration on July 6, 2026 backing water red lines (The Diplomat, 2026-07-11). No confirmed kinetic clash or deliberate physical flow cut-off has been executed; India's ability to cut flows remains 'technically limited' (CNBC, 2026-06-22).
water_dispute.rationale: The 1960 Indus Waters Treaty is officially suspended/contested and both sides have exchanged explicit official war threats tied directly to river control — satisfying rubric level 1 (treaty suspended, official threats exchanged). No confirmed armed clash or confirmed deliberate flow cut-off has occurred, so level 2 is not warranted. [vintage guard: new read is 2026-08-03 data but the prior applied value was 2026-08-17 data; kept the newer vintage]

dissent.view: Some analysts (New Lines Institute, Chatham House) characterize the situation as approaching crisis given nuclear-armed context and infrastructure acceleration, implying a borderline level-2 reading
GERD/Nile dispute also remains 'tense' (level 1): Egypt has raised the issue to the UN Security Council and accuses Ethiopia of violating international law, but no kinetic action has occurred

fao_food_trend.fact: FAO Food Price Index averaged 131.1 points in July 2026, up 0.6% MoM from June 2026 (130.3) and 1.0% above July 2025; highest reading since January 2023. Source: FAO official press release, fao.org/newsroom, released 2026-08-07.
fao_food_trend.rationale: The composite FFPI is rising both MoM (+0.6%) and YoY (+1.0%), placing it in the ELEVATED band; the MoM gain is well below the 3% upper boundary for band 1 and far below the 5% SPIKING threshold, even though sub-components (wheat +5.8%, sugar +6%) individually spiked.

china_export_curbs.fact: The NDRC suspended orderly phosphate fertilizer exports through August 2026 (NDRC special meeting, Dec 11 2025; confirmed by S&P Global Platts, Exiger, SunSirs, Fertilizer Daily Jul 29 2026). Urea exports were partially re-opened via a ~3 million tonne quota (issued May 26 2026) with an NDRC-mandated FOB price floor of $660/t for prilled and $670/t for granular urea, covering a June-August window (Profercy, Keyuan Fertilizer, May 26-29 2026). The last NEW product broadening (NK blends + additional phosphate varieties) occurred mid-March 2026 — outside the trailing 3-month window from Aug 24 2026.
china_export_curbs.rationale: Phosphate suspension and quota-controlled urea exports are ongoing as of today, satisfying rubric level 1 (existing restrictions unchanged). The last confirmed broadening action (mid-March NK blend ban) occurred ~5 months ago, outside the 3-month window required for level 2; no new or additional product categories have been restricted in the trailing 3 months (May 24 - Aug 24 2026).

dissent.view: Fertilizer Daily (Jul 29 2026) reports China 'extended' phosphate curbs through August 2026, which could be interpreted as a new tightening action if the extension was formally enacted post-May 24 — but the underlying suspension was set in Dec 2025 and the extension appears to be a continuation, not a new restriction on additional products.

hormuz_fertilizer.fact: straits.live (updated 2026-08-23): 'Effectively no, it is closed to commercial shipping as of 23 August 2026. 1 ship transited on August 16 vs ~73/day normal. Brent $94.39.' WTO Trade Tracker (late June 2026) confirms fertilizer-related outbound AIS flows 'remained absent or effectively at zero' even after the mid-June MoU, and CarraGlobe (July 2026) reports the MoU broke down in early July after fresh attacks. ITC/UN News (Aug 2026) records urea exports -83% and ammonia -75% YoY through April.
hormuz_fertilizer.rationale: The strait is physically rated CLOSED by real-time PortWatch/AIS data (1 transit/day vs 73 baseline), fertilizer/sulfur/ammonia outbound flows are at or near zero per WTO AXSMarine tracking, and Brent at ~$94 provides the required market corroboration - all three rubric conditions for a rating of 2 are met.

dissent.view: AgWeb/StoneX (July 14 2026) notes strait is 'technically still open' with some naval-escorted convoys moving, and summer fill prices for anhydrous ammonia and UAN had pulled back from spring highs - suggesting a partial flow rather than full cut

taiwan_tension.fact: Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense (MND) reported on Aug 16, 2026 detecting 11 PLA aircraft and 8 PLAN vessels operating around Taiwan, with 7 aircraft crossing the median line into northern and central ADIZ; similar daily incursions were recorded Aug 14-15. The most recent named large-scale drill was a two-day PLA live-fire exercise in the Taiwan Strait Jul 24-25, 2026 (SCMP, Jul 23 2026). Heritage Foundation/Daily Signal assessed as of Jul 31, 2026 that '2026 has witnessed a relative lull in coercive Chinese military activities around Taiwan' compared to late 2025 Justice Mission drills. No kinetic clash, blockade, or full mobilization has been reported.
taiwan_tension.rationale: Persistent daily median-line crossings and regular naval presence constitute assertive patrols above routine, meeting rubric level 1 (ELEVATED); the Jul 24-25 live-fire drill reinforces this. No blockade, kinetic engagement, or full mobilization evidence exists to justify level 2.

dissent.view: Heritage Foundation/Daily Signal (Jul 31, 2026) characterises 2026 activity as a 'relative lull' compared to late-2025 Justice Mission exercises, implying conditions closer to the lower end of level 1 or borderline level 0.
SecurityStudies.info (Aug 16, 2026) rates the situation explicitly 'Elevated' due to sustained gray-zone activities and regular ADIZ incursions, consistent with level 1.

export_controls.fact: US side: MATCH Act (introduced April 2, 2026) proposes blanket DUV lithography ban to China; VEU exemptions for Samsung/SK Hynix/TSMC/Micron revoked; Commerce Dept pressing ASML on EUV diversion since April 2026 (Reuters/CNBC, July 2026). China side: April 2026 Regulations on Countering Improper Extraterritorial Jurisdiction empowers Beijing to prohibit ASML-type FDP Rule compliance (Just Security, July 9, 2026); 2026 Import-Export Licensing Catalogue added rare-earth licensing controls (samarium, gadolinium, lutetium); NdPr benchmark +21.4% through July 1, 2026 as corroborating price signal (Tech-Insider, ~July 2026).
export_controls.rationale: Both sides have enacted new measures within the trailing 3-month window: the US through the MATCH Act legislative push and VEU revocations (tightening), and China through counter-jurisdiction regulations and expanded rare-earth export licensing (retaliation with a corroborating commodity price spike). Rubric level 2 (RETALIATION) is met: the target country has enacted active countermeasures including legal retaliation tools and input-supply controls.

dissent.view: East Asia Forum (March 2026) characterises the White House as having 'cooled' chip export controls and suspending further restrictions under Trump trade-talk priorities, suggesting the executive branch has partially softened enforcement even as Congress escalates -- this would cap the read closer to 1 if only executive action counts.

China-Briefing notes the October 2025 rare earth controls were suspended until November 10, 2026 per Xi-Trump Busan agreement, potentially weakening the retaliation signal for gallium/germanium specifically.

fab_concentration.fact: As of August 2026, all TSMC <=3nm capacity (2nm N2 at ~90,000-100,000 wpm in Fab 20/Fab 22 Taiwan; 3nm at Fab 18 Taiwan) is located in Taiwan. TSMC Arizona Fab 21 Phase 1 produces N4 (4nm) only; Phase 2 (N3/3nm) has completed construction but volume production is not targeted until H2 2027. TSMC Kumamoto Fab 2 (3nm) targets 2028. Zero operational <=3nm wafer capacity exists outside Taiwan. Source: tsmc.com/static/abouttsmcaz (updated ~July 2026); TSMC Q1 2026 earnings call (April 16 2026); TrendForce/Quantumrun June 2026.
fab_concentration.rationale: With all 2nm and 3nm production concentrated in Taiwan fabs and overseas <=3nm fabs not entering volume production until 2027-2028 at the earliest, the share of leading-edge capacity outside Taiwan is effectively 0% -- well below the rubric's 10% threshold -- and no operational overseas leading-edge fab exists, satisfying both EXTREME conditions.

dissent.view: TrendForce (Dec 2023 projection) estimated Taiwan would hold ~60% of advanced-node capacity (16nm and below) by 2027, implying a non-trivial share outside Taiwan by that date -- but this covers all advanced nodes (not strictly <=3nm) and refers to a future projection, not current 2026 operational status.

hormuz_redsea_status.fact: Lloyd's List Intelligence (Aug 19, 2026): 73 transits through Strait of Hormuz in week of Aug 10-16 vs ~138/day pre-conflict; the June 17 MoU expired Aug 17 without agreement, Iran resumed attacks on commercial vessels, U.S. blockade of Iranian ports active, yet non-Iranian traffic continues in both directions under U.S. naval escort. Brent crude ~$94-95/bbl (Trading Economics, Aug 21, 2026), elevated ~39% YoY but well below the April 30 closure-panic peak of $120.88. Red Sea: Houthi naval blockade of Saudi shipping declared July 20; Bab el-Mandeb transits down ~40% with lethal attacks ongoing (CNBC/CFR, Aug 12, 2026).
hormuz_redsea_status.rationale: Hormuz traffic is severely suppressed (~7% of pre-crisis daily rate) with active attacks and a blockade — well under 25% — but U.S. naval-escorted convoys continue moving non-Iranian cargo and Brent at ~$95 is elevated but not at the April closure-panic peak of $121, which the rubric requires to confirm a '2'. Both corridors are therefore CONTESTED (1): physically threatened, partially disrupted, moving under naval escort, with no functioning ceasefire or MoU in force.

dissent.view: straits.live (Aug 23, 2026) characterises the Strait as 'effectively closed to commercial shipping' citing 1 transit on Aug 16 vs ~73/day normal — a rating-2 framing; however this conflicts with Lloyd's List JMIC data showing 73 transits in the full week of Aug 10-16 and U.S. military convoy operations, so rubric caps at 1.

carraglobe.com (Jul 30, 2026) declares the Strait 'effectively closed to routine commercial shipping as of 30 July 2026'; however, subsequent Lloyd's List and EIA data show continued (if suppressed) non-Iranian transits and naval escorts, undermining a strict '2' read.

cable_incidents.fact: The PEACE submarine cable was cut in the Red Sea ~1,450km from Zafarana, Egypt, with repair expected to take 'several months' (Data Center Dynamics, ~July 2026, published ~1 month before 2026-08-24); separately, Geneva Solutions (2026-05-18) confirmed that of the four cables severed in the Sept 6 2025 Red Sea incident, 'one of which is still out of service' as of May 2026. At least two major Red Sea cables (PEACE + one from the Sept 2025 batch) are simultaneously severed and unrepaired.
cable_incidents.rationale: Rubric level 2 requires >=1 major cable currently severed and unrepaired causing connectivity loss, or multiple simultaneous cuts; the PEACE cable (cut ~July 2026, unrepaired) plus at least one residual unrepaired cable from the Sept 2025 event meet the 'multiple simultaneous' threshold. Hormuz cables face credible Iranian threats but no confirmed cut; Baltic incidents are anchor-drag suspicions without confirmed active outage, so those alone would rate 1, but the Red Sea picture drives the score to 2.

dissent.view: Hormuz cables face only threatened (not actual) damage: Iran IRGC-linked Tasnim issued warnings in April 2026 but 'no attack has yet taken place' (Jerusalem Post, 2026-04-23)
Baltic incidents as of Jan 2026 involve anchor-drag suspicions and detentions, not confirmed active cable outages (Euronews, 2026-01-12)

treasury_clearing_rollout.fact: SEC Commissioner Uyeda's August 7, 2026 statement confirms deadlines remain intact (cash 2026-12-31, repo 2027-06-30) but notes: (1) SIFMA and IIB exemptive-relief requests (inter-affiliate scope, non-U.S. transactions) are still pending SEC action after comment periods closed; (2) a new Rule 15c3-3 net-omnibus margin exemption is out for comment with a deadline of August 31, 2026; (3) documentation backlog persists — TBAC May 2026 report identifies bilateral legal agreements as 'the largest challenge from an implementation standpoint'; (4) industry expert Glenn Handley (SecFin Solutions, May 2026) wrote 'The infrastructure is not [ready].' DTCC's own FICC survey (July 2026) shows 'most' members already prepared or completing final readiness, but the fi-desk.com summary (August 2026) notes 'meaningful work remains.' No deadline extension has been granted; no operational test failure reported. Sources: SEC.gov Uyeda statement Aug 7 2026; TBAC Charge1Q2 2026 PDF (home.treasury.gov, May 2026); fi-desk.com Aug 2026; finadium.com FICC survey Jul 2026.
treasury_clearing_rollout.rationale: Multiple pending exemptive-relief requests (SIFMA inter-affiliate, IIB non-U.S., 15c3-3 margin), an explicit documentation/legal-agreement backlog flagged by TBAC, and industry skepticism about infrastructure readiness squarely match rubric level 1 (documentation backlog, pending exemptive relief). No deadline extension or operational failure justifies level 2, and the open relief requests and legal backlogs preclude level 0. [vintage guard: new read is 2026-08-07 data but the prior applied value was 2026-08 data; kept the newer vintage]

dissent.view: DTCC/FICC member survey (Jul 2026) reports 'most' full-service Netting Members already prepared or in final readiness activities, suggesting closer to smooth (level 0) for FICC direct participants
Industry practitioner Glenn Handley (SecFin Solutions, May 2026) argues infrastructure is not ready and deadlines are fixed but infrastructure lags, implying risk of level 2
